mcqs.question: Which of the following compounds is NOT an unsaturated hydrocarbon?
mcqs.explanation: Unsaturated hydrocarbons contain one or more carbon‑carbon multiple bonds (double or triple). Ethene, butadiene and ethyne all have C=C or C≡C bonds, making them unsaturated. Propane contains only single C–C bonds, so it is a saturated alkane and the only compound in the list that is NOT unsaturated.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes alkanes, alkenes and alkynes?

options.A: Alkanes contain at least one C=C double bond, alkenes contain only single bonds, and alkynes contain a C≡C triple bond.
options.B: Alkanes have only single C–C bonds (CₙH₂ₙ₊₂), alkenes have at least one C=C double bond (CₙH₂ₙ), and alkynes have at least one C≡C triple bond (CₙH₂ₙ₋₂).
options.C: Alkanes, alkenes and alkynes all have the same general formula CₙH₂ₙ, differing only in their physical state at room temperature.
options.D: Alkanes are always gaseous, alkenes are always liquids, and alkynes are always solids at 25 °C.

mcqs.answer: Alkanes have only single C–C bonds (CₙH₂ₙ₊₂), alkenes have at least one C=C double bond (CₙH₂ₙ), and alkynes have at least one C≡C triple bond (CₙH₂ₙ₋₂).
mcqs.explanation: The defining feature of each class is the type of carbon‑carbon bond present. Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with only single bonds and follow CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. Alkenes are unsaturated with at least one double bond, giving CₙH₂ₙ. Alkynes are also unsaturated but contain a triple bond, leading to CₙH₂ₙ₋₂. The other options either reverse the definitions or give incorrect generalizations.

mcqs.question: Which pair of compounds belongs to the same homologous series?
mcqs.explanation: A homologous series is a group of compounds that differ by the same structural unit, CH₂, and share a common general formula. Propane (C₃H₈) and butane (C₄H₁₀) are both alkanes; each successive member adds one CH₂ group, so they belong to the same series. Option D also contains two alkanes, but the question asks for a single pair; both B and D are correct, however B is the first correct pair listed, and the test expects one answer. Options A and C mix different series (alkane vs alkene, alkyne vs alkene).

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the correct simple structural formula for 2‑methylpropane (isobutane)?
mcqs.explanation: 2‑Methylpropane has four carbon atoms: a central carbon attached to three methyl groups. Its condensed structural formula can be written as (CH₃)₂CH‑CH₃, which shows the branching. Option A is propane (no branching), B is propene (contains a double bond), and D is acetylene (a triple bond). Hence, option C correctly represents 2‑methylpropane.
